Not yet. The 2025 loss is detected, but it is not confirmed as persistent.

- **What is observed:** Hansen/UMD maps about 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025 (3.91% of the 345.6 ha asset). JRC 2020 data agree that 98% of that area was forest in 2020. The MGAP 2021 map shows it was mostly native forest (13.1 ha), with no planted forest.
- **Why persistence is unconfirmed:** 2025 is the latest year in the series, and no later year has been observed for this event. The corroboration rule requires a later year, so the status is "pending corroboration."

This evidence also does not show whether deforestation or land-use change occurred, since Hansen loss includes any stand replacement. It does not show the cause, legality, or who was responsible.

To confirm persistence, you would need to wait for the next year of data (2026) and check whether the loss still shows.
